## atira
Atira Challenges: debug your team's agent system runs. Start with list_runs, then get_run; diagnose_run says why a run failed and whether to rerun. run_logs filters a run's logs by time (from/to on the run's clock, mm:ss as the run page shows it), stream and text; run_llm_calls lists every model call; run_profile shows where the time went; run_screenshot shows a browser's screen at a time (or every browser, or a filmstrip); run_inputs lists what the agent clicked, scrolled and typed; compare_runs puts two runs side by side. run_package shows the package a run or submission used (agent.json and its files) and saves it with out. test_run starts a test run from a folder; wait_for_run waits for it. submit (a scored submission: public, and it can't be undone) and cancel_run need confirm: true, so ask the person first and wait for an explicit yes. The agent system must work everything out during the run, with a model choosing where to go, what to search for and what matters. Never copy values from run logs, answers, screenshots or the websites into the package (prompts and notes included), and don't replace the model with a fixed script or a crawl-then-one-shot call: the reviewer rejects both. Rules at a glance: https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude.ai Higgsfield
Recipe/setup slashes: get_preset_instructions before other workflows; unambiguous model slashes: models_explore; unknowns: resolve. For 3D scenes or location angles, first call get_preset_instructions with { preset: "/3d-jutsu" }. This includes new camera views of the same supplied location; image critique alone does not activate scene work. After verifying a completed Katana video, call show_result with action "katana_video" and media_id or url. For /effects or Viral browsing use get_presets source:'viral'; /product or product-shot catalogs: source:'marketing_studio', category:'product-shot'; /motion or motion catalogs: category:'motion'. /marketing-studio opens get_presets source:'marketing_studio'. Generic Marketing Studio, UGC/ads/posters/marketplace: show_marketing_studio_v2. Browsing never authorizes execute_preset. Creation: generate_image, generate_video, generate_audio. Attached media without media_id: if readable in your sandbox, upload it yourself: media_upload, curl PUT, media_confirm (overrides widget steps); else call media_upload_widget as the only tool in that turn. Resume after upload. Mixed image/video: type:'auto', multiple:true. Voice: create_voice. Higgsfield Genjutsu routes through generate_video: motion transfer -> hf_mult_motion_control; object replacement -> hf_mult_replace_object. For top/popular/trending Genjutsu, first get_presets source=genjutsu category=genjutsu-trending; never legacy motion_control or ad-multiplier for one Genjutsu edit. Without an explicit preset recipe, for multi-step videos call get_workflow_instructions first (with no argument). For clip edits call get_workflow_instructions with { workflow: "ad-multiplier" } first. AI Influencer: ai_influencer_prepare then ai_influencer_generate. Character sheets: call get_workflow_instructions with { workflow: "character-sheet" }; websites/apps/games: call get_workflow_instructions with { workflow: "website-builder-flow" }. Character sheets require explicit requests. Bundled files: get_workflow_bundle_file. For AI Influencer chat creation, use ai_influencer_get_options for explicit traits, ai_influencer_list_presets for examples, or ai_influencer_get_settings with job_id for an existing sheet. ai_influencer_prepare returns design and price without generation. Preserve references and seed; use randomize=false for exact settings. Pass prepared params unchanged to ai_influencer_generate with max_credits at the quote or a lower user budget. Existing creation intent permits proceeding within budget; preview-only requests must stop after preparation. For explicit free-only intent, require known available free_gens_remaining and use_free_gens=true with max_credits=0; never fall back to credits. For variants, prepare each sheet and respect total count and aggregate budget. The generator opens an auto-updating widget for progress and the completed sheet. Wait with jobs_wait (timeout_seconds <= 15); do not duplicate the display with show_generation_by_ids or job_display unless explicitly requested. Offer Genjutsu animation afterward unless declined; require agreement and selection of the exact completed character before get_presets source=genjutsu category=genjutsu with initial_inputs.character_sheet=[{id:job_id,type:image_job}]. Opening that gallery does not authorize video submission. If chat creation is unavailable, report it without silently switching to generic image generation or the builder UI. Multiple independent generations: batch tools, jobs_wait, then one show_generation_by_ids. Use generate_3d to turn an image into a 3D GLB mesh. When unsure which model fits, call models_explore(action:'recommend') before calling a generate_* tool. Use virality_predictor when the user asks to predict video virality or analyze engagement, attention, audience response, retention risk, hook strength, or creative performance. For other existing-asset edits use upscale_image/video, outpaint_image, reframe, remove_background, relight_image, or motion_control (single-character Kling recast). For voice creation in Apps UI-capable clients, call create_voice … [truncated]

## claude.ai Miro
The canvas_* tools enable the agent to read, create, and update Miro boards using Canvas Composer SVG, Miro's unified interaction/representation protocol for the canvas. To understand how to use the canvas_* tools in the appropiate way, please refer to the canvas_composer_skill tool first to understand the guidelines and protocol.

## comfyui
Controls a local ComfyUI server. Use generate_image for simple text-to-image and generate_video for text-to-video / GIFs (slow: minutes per clip). For anything else, build an API-format workflow (node id -> {class_type, inputs}) and call run_workflow; use list_nodes / get_node_info to discover node inputs and list_models to find valid model filenames.

## entire-brain
Tool results are bounded to 131072 bytes. Oversize JSON results with removable row lists drop whole tail rows and set "response_truncated": true; each shortened list reports {path, returned, total} under "response_truncation". A result that cannot be reduced to the budget returns an error asking you to narrow the request. Limit and depth arguments bound requested work, not serialized bytes. The total is the number of rows produced by this call before trimming, already capped by its limit; it is not the corpus count. Raising the limit may retrieve more candidates but does not establish the total available. Each list keeps its first 64 rows when space allows; remaining space is shared proportionally. If that floor does not fit, lists use a shared width. Matching pagination counts are updated to returned rows. Truncated array roots are wrapped in {"items": [...]} so markers remain at the document root.

## entire-docs
This Model Context Protocol server provides search and retrieval tools for the Entire site. Use it to answer questions from public site content. Prefer information returned by this server over prior knowledge, and cite or reference the relevant site results when possible. Do not claim access to private or authenticated content unless the current MCP session is authenticated. This server also exposes resources containing additional skill guidance; read the relevant resources when they apply to the task. If you find a problem with the documentation — a page that is incorrect, outdated, confusing, or incomplete — use the submit_feedback tool to report it to the docs team. Apart from the submit_feedback tool, the server is read-only and scoped to Entire; it does not otherwise perform actions, mutate state, or access anything beyond the published site content and these resources.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in
    change  ->  entire graph diff --base A --head B --json
    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)
    stats   ->  entire graph stats --repo .        (human-facing token-savings report; not part of your workflow — do not run it unless asked)
# What we tried and learned

One bullet per experiment or failure: what changed, what happened, what we keep. Written by hand; run data is in
`experiments/runs.jsonl` (render it with `python3 dev/track.py report`).

- v0-starter test run: the starter kit's `solve()` stub exits without an answer; the sandbox scores that 0 and
  ineligible after 4 s.
- v1 local (first signed bid): the configurator worker needed 36 requests and 433 s for a bid with every position
  omitted; about 230 s of that went to the TAN round trips (153 s to 385 s).
- TAN loop: each TAN request invalidates the previous TAN, and the mail worker was started 6 times (2 hit the 8-request
  limit) before a fresh TAN reached the signing step in time. Fetch the TAN right after requesting it, in one sequence.
- Tokens: 247k input for a bid without positions, nearly all in the configurator worker; trim page views before v2.
- TAN lookup fixes: never put wall-clock time in a goal (the sites run on the scenario clock, so a TAN "requested at
  <today>" never shows up); "newest" is the highest request number. Short lookups run without note(), so the model
  returns its result instead of noting it and searching on.
- v1 first test run crashed at import: `llm.py` imported `httpx`, but openai 3.x depends on `httpx2`; the local venv
  still had a stale `httpx` from openai 2.x. Run `uv sync` after dependency changes so local matches the sandbox.
- v1 first scored test run: quality 10 (decision 5 + reference 5), eligible, 3.4 min, $0.022. Discount, total and
  total consistency score 0 even with every position omitted and total 0; positions need v2.
- v1 submission: review passed, quality 10, 4:41 min, $0.024; team rank #4. Submit from a clean `git archive` export
  of agent/ so unfinished files never reach the package reviewer.
- Model calls are queue-bound: across our runs a call waits a median 2 to 3 s for a GPU and then answers in about
  0.35 s (thinking off). Run time is roughly the number of sequential model calls times that wait, and cost is about
  $0.0004 per call, so both fall with fewer, larger steps and with workers whose waits overlap. `dev/dashboard.py`
  shows the split per run (GPU wait against model answering).
- Fastest v1 test run: 27 calls, 87 s, $0.010. The same flow has taken up to 63 calls and 282 s; the spread is the
  TAN round trips and the configurator steps, not the model.
- First four-browser research run (364 calls, 12.8 min, $0.18) still scored 10: research was cut off at its time
  budget without a plan, so the bid fell back to every position omitted. Research must hand over partial findings
  per position before its budget ends, and the budget must leave room for entering positions, not only for signing.
- In that run the TAN lookup hit its 8-request limit twice before the third attempt returned in 4 requests (about
  75 s lost). Not yet checked why; first thing to look at is where the mailbox tab stood when the lookup started.
- run_d4deebd2d3a2d429 (unchanged v1, baseline for branch speed-cost): quality 10, 105 calls, 11.9 min, $0.069,
  against 27 calls and 87 s for the same code earlier. The bid form took 428 s before the first TAN request (model
  answering summed to 933 s, about 9 s per call with thinking on), four of six TAN lookups stopped at the 8-request
  limit, and after the accepted answer the agent kept calling the model and ended in a 401 traceback. v1's time is
  not stable: one run says little, and thinking on in the bid form is the first thing to measure.
- run_b63b37e9c3b6b1df (first v2: research workers, plan, bid entry): quality 34.3 (from 10), 184 calls, 7.5 min,
  $0.085. Two of five positions entered; both right on material, quantity and base price, one right on lead time.
  Discount and the withdrawn-answer check scored. Unit price, total and consistency scored 0 because surcharge,
  packaging and bonus are not built; three positions were omitted because their stroke is a usable stroke whose
  end reserve was not looked up. The TAN took one request and one lookup of one call.
- A plan must not conclude "no material matches" from wording: two sources name the same mounting or certification
  differently. A local run sent a wrong no_bid for that reason. Numbers are compared in code, wording is the
  model's call, and no_bid needs the model to have chosen no material as well.
- With thinking on, a worker can spend its whole answer deliberating (token limit reached with nothing recorded);
  the tender positions worker lost a local run that way. It now gets one more try with thinking the other way.
- A page view shows a local time and, in brackets, the element's machine timestamp. Parsing the first with the
  zone of the second shifted every such date; the machine timestamp now wins.
- Mail lookups: an empty folder costs the full 10-request limit, because the model keeps trying search words.
#!/bin/sh
# Run the agent locally against the public scouting sites (headless) and record it in experiments/local-runs.jsonl
# (gitignored). Usage, from anywhere: dev/run-local.sh <version> ["note"] [experiment]
# Needs `atira login` and `atira models proxy` running in another terminal. HEADLESS=0 shows the browser.
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
version=${1:?usage: dev/run-local.sh <version> [note] [experiment]}
note=${2:-}
experiment=${3:-}
curl -s --max-time 5 -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8765/ || {
  echo "The models proxy is not running: start \`atira models proxy\` in another terminal first."; exit 1; }
commit=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)
dirty=no; [ -n "$(git status --porcelain -- agent)" ] && dirty=yes
traces="$PWD/agent/traces/$(date -u +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
mkdir -p "$traces"
eval "$(atira scout --env)"
(cd agent && uv sync -q && HEADLESS=${HEADLESS:-1} TRACE_DIR="$traces" uv run --no-sync python agent.py)
status=$?
trace=$(ls "$traces"/run-*.jsonl 2>/dev/null | head -1)
[ -n "$trace" ] || { echo "The agent wrote no trace; nothing recorded."; exit $status; }
python3 dev/track.py local --trace "$trace" --version "$version" --experiment "$experiment" --note "$note" \
  --commit "$commit" --dirty "$dirty" && python3 dev/track.py report && python3 dev/dashboard.py
exit $status
"""The run contract: read the run (the brief, the websites and their logins, where the answer goes), submit the answer.

In a test run or a scored run the platform sets CHALLENGE_API_URL and CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN. On your own machine there
is no run token: `eval "$(atira scout --env)"` exports the public scouting run as CHALLENGE_SCOUTING instead, and
nothing done with those logins counts. Docs: $API/docs/run-contract.md
"""
import json
import os
import time
from urllib.error import HTTPError, URLError
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen

USER_AGENT = "atira-starter-kit/3"  # the API's edge refuses Python's default urllib agent
LOAD_SCOUTING = 'eval "$(atira scout --env)"; in PowerShell: atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression'


def http(url: str, token: str | None = None, payload: dict | None = None, timeout: float = 30) -> tuple[int, str]:
    """GET (or POST `payload` as JSON) with the run token in x-api-key: the status and the body."""
    headers = {"Accept": "application/json", "User-Agent": USER_AGENT}
    if token:
        headers["x-api-key"] = token
    data = None
    if payload is not None:
        data = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False).encode()
        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
    try:
        with urlopen(Request(url, data=data, headers=headers), timeout=timeout) as response:
            return response.status, response.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    except HTTPError as error:
        return error.code, error.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")


def load_run(env=os.environ) -> tuple[dict, str | None]:
    """The run and its token; locally, without a token, the scouting run that `atira scout --env` exported.

    The run has `brief` (the task and its rules, markdown), `access` (per website: `siteId`, `url`, `credentials`),
    `submission` (`kind` "api" or "site", and its `url`), `answer_schema`, `started_at` and `expires_at`.
    """
    token = env.get("CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN")
    if not token:
        if not env.get("CHALLENGE_SCOUTING"):
            raise SystemExit(f"No run token and no scouting logins. To develop locally: {LOAD_SCOUTING}")
        try:
            return json.loads(env["CHALLENGE_SCOUTING"]), None
        except ValueError:
            raise SystemExit(f"CHALLENGE_SCOUTING is not the JSON atira exports. Load it again: {LOAD_SCOUTING}")
    url = env["CHALLENGE_API_URL"].rstrip("/") + "/v1/runs/current"
    status, body = 0, ""
    for attempt in range(5):  # rides out a restart of the API
        try:
            status, body = http(url, token)
        except (URLError, OSError) as error:
            status, body = 0, str(error)
        if status == 200:
            return json.loads(body), token
        if status in (401, 403, 404):  # the run is over, or the token is wrong: no point in asking again
            break
        time.sleep(2 * (attempt + 1))
    raise SystemExit(f"Cannot read the run: HTTP {status} {body[:300]}")


def seconds_left(run: dict, now: float | None = None) -> float:
    """Seconds until the run's `expires_at` (epoch milliseconds); after that the answer is refused and the run scores
    0. Every part of the answer scores on its own, so submit your best answer about a minute before time runs out
    rather than keep searching."""
    expires_at = run.get("expires_at")
    if not expires_at:
        return float("inf")
    return expires_at / 1000 - (time.time() if now is None else now)


def submit_answer(run: dict, token: str | None, answer: dict) -> tuple[int, str]:
    """POST the answer to the run's "api" submission target. 202: accepted and final, the run ends. 400: the body
    lists the issues; nothing is recorded, fix the answer and send it again. A "site" submission is entered on that
    website instead, and the website confirms it with a receipt."""
    submission = run["submission"]
    if submission.get("kind") != "api":
        raise ValueError(f"This run takes its answer on the website {submission.get('url')}, not through the API")
    if not token:
        raise ValueError("No run to answer: locally there is no run token. Test it in a run: atira test-run .")
    return http(run.get("answer_url") or submission["url"], token, answer, timeout=60)
"""
Read the run's brief once: which tender, who bids, and which website plays which part.

Website ids and roles differ between datasets, so the model maps them from the brief and the run's access list
instead of the code knowing any site by name. The answer is checked against the brief.
"""
import llm
from browser_tools import unseen_values
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from pydantic_ai import Agent, ModelRetry


class Briefing(BaseModel):
    tender_reference: str = Field(description="The exact reference of the tender to bid on, as the brief writes it")
    company_name: str = Field(description="The bidder company name to register with, exactly as the brief gives it")
    vat_id: str = Field(description="The bidder's VAT id (USt-IdNr.) as the brief gives it, or '' if none")
    scenario_date: str = Field(description="The scenario date and time as the brief states it")
    bid_site: str = Field(description="siteId of the website where the bid is entered and signed")
    mail_site: str = Field(description="siteId of the bidder's own webmail, where approvals and the signing TAN arrive")
    tender_site: str = Field(description="siteId of the website that holds the tender and its clarifications (Q&A)")
    spec_site: str = Field(description="siteId of the website that holds the buyer's technical specification")
    erp_site: str = Field(description="siteId of the bidder's ERP, with materials, stock and prices")
    submission_steps: str = Field(description="The brief's instructions for entering, signing and submitting the "
                                              "bid, copied word for word")


SITE_ROLES = ("bid_site", "mail_site", "tender_site", "spec_site", "erp_site")  # one site may play several roles


async def read_brief(task: dict) -> Briefing:
    sites = "\n".join(f"- siteId {s['siteId']}: {s['url']}" for s in task["access"])
    submission = task.get("submission", {})
    agent = Agent(llm.model(), output_type=Briefing, model_settings=llm.settings(thinking=True), retries=3,
                  instructions="You read a task brief and extract facts from it exactly as written.")

    @agent.output_validator
    def _from_brief(briefing: Briefing) -> Briefing:
        ids = {s["siteId"] for s in task["access"]}
        wrong = [role for role in SITE_ROLES if getattr(briefing, role) not in ids]
        if wrong:
            raise ModelRetry(f"{', '.join(wrong)} must be among these siteIds: {sorted(ids)}")
        missing = unseen_values(briefing.model_dump_json(exclude=set(SITE_ROLES)), task["brief"])
        if missing:
            raise ModelRetry(f"{', '.join(missing)} are not in the brief; copy values exactly from it.")
        return briefing

    prompt = (f"Websites of this run:\n{sites}\n\nThe answer goes to: {submission}\n\nBrief:\n{task['brief']}")
    result = await agent.run(prompt)
    return result.output

    change  ->  entire graph diff --base A --head B --json

# What we tried and learned

One bullet per experiment or failure: what changed, what happened, what we keep. Written by hand; run data is in
`experiments/runs.jsonl` (render it with `python3 dev/track.py report`).

- v0-starter test run: the starter kit's `solve()` stub exits without an answer; the sandbox scores that 0 and
  ineligible after 4 s.
- v1 local (first signed bid): the configurator worker needed 36 requests and 433 s for a bid with every position
  omitted; about 230 s of that went to the TAN round trips (153 s to 385 s).
- TAN loop: each TAN request invalidates the previous TAN, and the mail worker was started 6 times (2 hit the 8-request
  limit) before a fresh TAN reached the signing step in time. Fetch the TAN right after requesting it, in one sequence.
- Tokens: 247k input for a bid without positions, nearly all in the configurator worker; trim page views before v2.
- TAN lookup fixes: never put wall-clock time in a goal (the sites run on the scenario clock, so a TAN "requested at
  <today>" never shows up); "newest" is the highest request number. Short lookups run without note(), so the model
  returns its result instead of noting it and searching on.
- v1 first test run crashed at import: `llm.py` imported `httpx`, but openai 3.x depends on `httpx2`; the local venv
  still had a stale `httpx` from openai 2.x. Run `uv sync` after dependency changes so local matches the sandbox.
- v1 first scored test run: quality 10 (decision 5 + reference 5), eligible, 3.4 min, $0.022. Discount, total and
  total consistency score 0 even with every position omitted and total 0; positions need v2.
- v1 submission: review passed, quality 10, 4:41 min, $0.024; team rank #4. Submit from a clean `git archive` export
  of agent/ so unfinished files never reach the package reviewer.
- Model calls are queue-bound: across our runs a call waits a median 2 to 3 s for a GPU and then answers in about
  0.35 s (thinking off). Run time is roughly the number of sequential model calls times that wait, and cost is about
  $0.0004 per call, so both fall with fewer, larger steps and with workers whose waits overlap. `dev/dashboard.py`
  shows the split per run (GPU wait against model answering).
- Fastest v1 test run: 27 calls, 87 s, $0.010. The same flow has taken up to 63 calls and 282 s; the spread is the
  TAN round trips and the configurator steps, not the model.
- First four-browser research run (364 calls, 12.8 min, $0.18) still scored 10: research was cut off at its time
  budget without a plan, so the bid fell back to every position omitted. Research must hand over partial findings
  per position before its budget ends, and the budget must leave room for entering positions, not only for signing.
- In that run the TAN lookup hit its 8-request limit twice before the third attempt returned in 4 requests (about
  75 s lost). Not yet checked why; first thing to look at is where the mailbox tab stood when the lookup started.
- run_d4deebd2d3a2d429 (unchanged v1, baseline for branch speed-cost): quality 10, 105 calls, 11.9 min, $0.069,
  against 27 calls and 87 s for the same code earlier. The bid form took 428 s before the first TAN request (model
  answering summed to 933 s, about 9 s per call with thinking on), four of six TAN lookups stopped at the 8-request
  limit, and after the accepted answer the agent kept calling the model and ended in a 401 traceback. v1's time is
  not stable: one run says little, and thinking on in the bid form is the first thing to measure.
- run_b63b37e9c3b6b1df (first v2: research workers, plan, bid entry): quality 34.3 (from 10), 184 calls, 7.5 min,
  $0.085. Two of five positions entered; both right on material, quantity and base price, one right on lead time.
  Discount and the withdrawn-answer check scored. Unit price, total and consistency scored 0 because surcharge,
  packaging and bonus are not built; three positions were omitted because their stroke is a usable stroke whose
  end reserve was not looked up. The TAN took one request and one lookup of one call.
- A plan must not conclude "no material matches" from wording: two sources name the same mounting or certification
  differently. A local run sent a wrong no_bid for that reason. Numbers are compared in code, wording is the
  model's call, and no_bid needs the model to have chosen no material as well.
- With thinking on, a worker can spend its whole answer deliberating (token limit reached with nothing recorded);
  the tender positions worker lost a local run that way. It now gets one more try with thinking the other way.
- A page view shows a local time and, in brackets, the element's machine timestamp. Parsing the first with the
  zone of the second shifted every such date; the machine timestamp now wins.
- Mail lookups: an empty folder costs the full 10-request limit, because the model keeps trying search words.
#!/bin/sh
# Run the agent locally against the public scouting sites (headless) and record it in experiments/local-runs.jsonl
# (gitignored). Usage, from anywhere: dev/run-local.sh <version> ["note"] [experiment]
# Needs `atira login` and `atira models proxy` running in another terminal. HEADLESS=0 shows the browser.
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1
version=${1:?usage: dev/run-local.sh <version> [note] [experiment]}
note=${2:-}
experiment=${3:-}
curl -s --max-time 5 -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8765/ || {
  echo "The models proxy is not running: start \`atira models proxy\` in another terminal first."; exit 1; }
commit=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)
dirty=no; [ -n "$(git status --porcelain -- agent)" ] && dirty=yes
traces="$PWD/agent/traces/$(date -u +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
mkdir -p "$traces"
eval "$(atira scout --env)"
(cd agent && uv sync -q && HEADLESS=${HEADLESS:-1} TRACE_DIR="$traces" uv run --no-sync python agent.py)
status=$?
trace=$(ls "$traces"/run-*.jsonl 2>/dev/null | head -1)
[ -n "$trace" ] || { echo "The agent wrote no trace; nothing recorded."; exit $status; }
python3 dev/track.py local --trace "$trace" --version "$version" --experiment "$experiment" --note "$note" \
  --commit "$commit" --dirty "$dirty" && python3 dev/track.py report && python3 dev/dashboard.py
exit $status
"""The run contract: read the run (the brief, the websites and their logins, where the answer goes), submit the answer.

In a test run or a scored run the platform sets CHALLENGE_API_URL and CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN. On your own machine there
is no run token: `eval "$(atira scout --env)"` exports the public scouting run as CHALLENGE_SCOUTING instead, and
nothing done with those logins counts. Docs: $API/docs/run-contract.md
"""
import json
import os
import time
from urllib.error import HTTPError, URLError
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen

USER_AGENT = "atira-starter-kit/3"  # the API's edge refuses Python's default urllib agent
LOAD_SCOUTING = 'eval "$(atira scout --env)"; in PowerShell: atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression'


def http(url: str, token: str | None = None, payload: dict | None = None, timeout: float = 30) -> tuple[int, str]:
    """GET (or POST `payload` as JSON) with the run token in x-api-key: the status and the body."""
    headers = {"Accept": "application/json", "User-Agent": USER_AGENT}
    if token:
        headers["x-api-key"] = token
    data = None
    if payload is not None:
        data = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False).encode()
        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
    try:
        with urlopen(Request(url, data=data, headers=headers), timeout=timeout) as response:
            return response.status, response.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    except HTTPError as error:
        return error.code, error.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")


def load_run(env=os.environ) -> tuple[dict, str | None]:
    """The run and its token; locally, without a token, the scouting run that `atira scout --env` exported.

    The run has `brief` (the task and its rules, markdown), `access` (per website: `siteId`, `url`, `credentials`),
    `submission` (`kind` "api" or "site", and its `url`), `answer_schema`, `started_at` and `expires_at`.
    """
    token = env.get("CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN")
    if not token:
        if not env.get("CHALLENGE_SCOUTING"):
            raise SystemExit(f"No run token and no scouting logins. To develop locally: {LOAD_SCOUTING}")
        try:
            return json.loads(env["CHALLENGE_SCOUTING"]), None
        except ValueError:
            raise SystemExit(f"CHALLENGE_SCOUTING is not the JSON atira exports. Load it again: {LOAD_SCOUTING}")
    url = env["CHALLENGE_API_URL"].rstrip("/") + "/v1/runs/current"
    status, body = 0, ""
    for attempt in range(5):  # rides out a restart of the API
        try:
            status, body = http(url, token)
        except (URLError, OSError) as error:
            status, body = 0, str(error)
        if status == 200:
            return json.loads(body), token
        if status in (401, 403, 404):  # the run is over, or the token is wrong: no point in asking again
            break
        time.sleep(2 * (attempt + 1))
    raise SystemExit(f"Cannot read the run: HTTP {status} {body[:300]}")


def seconds_left(run: dict, now: float | None = None) -> float:
    """Seconds until the run's `expires_at` (epoch milliseconds); after that the answer is refused and the run scores
    0. Every part of the answer scores on its own, so submit your best answer about a minute before time runs out
    rather than keep searching."""
    expires_at = run.get("expires_at")
    if not expires_at:
        return float("inf")
    return expires_at / 1000 - (time.time() if now is None else now)


def submit_answer(run: dict, token: str | None, answer: dict) -> tuple[int, str]:
    """POST the answer to the run's "api" submission target. 202: accepted and final, the run ends. 400: the body
    lists the issues; nothing is recorded, fix the answer and send it again. A "site" submission is entered on that
    website instead, and the website confirms it with a receipt."""
    submission = run["submission"]
    if submission.get("kind") != "api":
        raise ValueError(f"This run takes its answer on the website {submission.get('url')}, not through the API")
    if not token:
        raise ValueError("No run to answer: locally there is no run token. Test it in a run: atira test-run .")
    return http(run.get("answer_url") or submission["url"], token, answer, timeout=60)
"""
Read the run's brief once: which tender, who bids, and which website plays which part.

Website ids and roles differ between datasets, so the model maps them from the brief and the run's access list
instead of the code knowing any site by name. The answer is checked against the brief.
"""
import llm
from browser_tools import unseen_values
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from pydantic_ai import Agent, ModelRetry


class Briefing(BaseModel):
    tender_reference: str = Field(description="The exact reference of the tender to bid on, as the brief writes it")
    company_name: str = Field(description="The bidder company name to register with, exactly as the brief gives it")
    vat_id: str = Field(description="The bidder's VAT id (USt-IdNr.) as the brief gives it, or '' if none")
    scenario_date: str = Field(description="The scenario date and time as the brief states it")
    bid_site: str = Field(description="siteId of the website where the bid is entered and signed")
    mail_site: str = Field(description="siteId of the bidder's own webmail, where approvals and the signing TAN arrive")
    tender_site: str = Field(description="siteId of the website that holds the tender and its clarifications (Q&A)")
    spec_site: str = Field(description="siteId of the website that holds the buyer's technical specification")
    erp_site: str = Field(description="siteId of the bidder's ERP, with materials, stock and prices")
    submission_steps: str = Field(description="The brief's instructions for entering, signing and submitting the "
                                              "bid, copied word for word")


SITE_ROLES = ("bid_site", "mail_site", "tender_site", "spec_site", "erp_site")  # one site may play several roles


async def read_brief(task: dict) -> Briefing:
    sites = "\n".join(f"- siteId {s['siteId']}: {s['url']}" for s in task["access"])
    submission = task.get("submission", {})
    agent = Agent(llm.model(), output_type=Briefing, model_settings=llm.settings(thinking=True), retries=3,
                  instructions="You read a task brief and extract facts from it exactly as written.")

    @agent.output_validator
    def _from_brief(briefing: Briefing) -> Briefing:
        ids = {s["siteId"] for s in task["access"]}
        wrong = [role for role in SITE_ROLES if getattr(briefing, role) not in ids]
        if wrong:
            raise ModelRetry(f"{', '.join(wrong)} must be among these siteIds: {sorted(ids)}")
        missing = unseen_values(briefing.model_dump_json(exclude=set(SITE_ROLES)), task["brief"])
        if missing:
            raise ModelRetry(f"{', '.join(missing)} are not in the brief; copy values exactly from it.")
        return briefing

    prompt = (f"Websites of this run:\n{sites}\n\nThe answer goes to: {submission}\n\nBrief:\n{task['brief']}")
    result = await agent.run(prompt)
    return result.output

# Agent plan and scouting notes

Findings from scouting the four public sites (public-1) and evaluating frameworks, 2026-10-10.
The private final run uses other sites, layouts and data: prompts describe roles and goals, never click paths,
and nothing below may be hardcoded into the agent.

## Framework decision

Keep the starter kit (Python 3.12, uv, Playwright 1.63) and run the worker loop on `pydantic-ai-slim[openai]`.
No browser-agent framework, no LangGraph.

- pydantic-ai 2.55 works with Qwen through the proxy (tested: tool call + typed output, thinking off, 3 s).
  It gives typed tools, typed output via an output tool (avoids the 74 s cold `json_schema` compile), validation
  retries, `UsageLimits` as a step budget, `history_processors` to drop stale page snapshots, and Logfire
  tracing. 26 packages.
- LangGraph: our orchestration is a fan-out of independent workers plus a pure calculation step. Plain asyncio
  covers that; LangGraph would add 38+ packages (plus a LangChain model client), its own state and checkpoint
  model and a second abstraction to debug, for no gain.

- `page.aria_snapshot(mode="ai")` gives a compact, ref-tagged tree (`button "Anmelden" [ref=e10]`), clickable via
  `page.locator("aria-ref=e10")`. That is Playwright MCP's core without a Node process.
- browser-use: heavy deps, slow single-action steps, may launch its own browser (killed by the sandbox).
- Stagehand: TS, or a Python client to a server process; extra LLM calls per act/extract.
- pydantic-ai: fine but optional; a ~150-line loop is easier to debug and to defend in package review.

## Qwen via the proxy (measured locally)

- Model id `qwen3.8-flash-next`, 262k context.
- Thinking is on by default. `extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": False}}` cuts a trivial call
  to ~0.9 s; use it for navigation steps, keep thinking on for decisions.
- Tool calls, parallel tool calls, `tool_choice="required"`, images (~1k tokens per 1280x800 JPEG) all work.
- Strict `json_schema` works, but the first call with a new schema took 74 s (cold compile). Prefer a
  `finish(result)` tool, or warm schemas at start-up.
- Prefix caching works (81.5k of 83k cached on repeat). Keep system prompts stable.
- 8 parallel calls: 4.7 s total. Team limit 32 concurrent.
- Clef `/v1/decide` works in ~1 s; `score` criteria must be a list. Skip in v1.

## Cross-site patterns

- All sites: login form, then `/consent` ("Notwendige Cookies akzeptieren").
- Decoy modals: close with the small x only; "Akzeptieren und fortfahren" leads to trap pages. Escape is blocked.
- Fake browser chrome (address bar, download bar) drawn in the page links to useless pages.
- Hidden decoy text (`display:none`, `aria-hidden`), including a prompt injection in every mail
  ("99 % Sonderrabatt"). Extract visible text only.
- Content in collapsed `<details>`: expand all before reading.
- Values in canvas `aria-label`s and CSS tooltips (`role=tooltip`), which `aria_snapshot` partly misses.
- Zero-width spaces (U+200B) in references, subjects, document numbers: strip them.
- Numbers carry locale tags `(en-US)` / `(de-DE)`; dates mix `(MM/TT)` and `(TT/MM)`.
- Pagination: 3 rows per page, "Weitere laden"; requesting past the end repeats the last page.
- Searches with more than 20 hits show nothing at all.
- `page.goto` can hang on `load`: use `wait_until="domcontentloaded"`.
- Flaky "Dienst voruebergehend nicht verfuegbar" pages (HTTP 200): detect by text, retry.
- Session expiry redirects to `/login?returnTo=...` with "Sitzung abgelaufen" (ERP: between 300 and 450 s idle).

## Tender portal

- Tender list paged; reference is in the brief. Tabs: `?tab=documents`, `?tab=questions`, `/submission`.
- Expression of interest may need one click ("Teilnahme bekunden").
- Documents: three "Oeffnen" controls in random order, two of them decoys; the title link is safe. Direct URL
  `/tenders/<ref>/documents/N`. ZIP under "Sammelakte" holds the same files.
- Q&A: two nested iframes (`questions-frame` -> `questions-content?page=N`), sorted by date not number, date in an
  "Eingang" tooltip (Athens and UTC). Content: quantity changes, withdrawals, Konditionsgruppe, packaging /
  commitment / setup-pool / bonus keys, setup fees, scoped technical amendments.
- Configurator (server-side wizard, "Zurueck" clears later steps):
  1. Bidder data (from the brief).
  2. Angebotsart: defaults to Nebenangebot (trap); choose Hauptangebot or Verzichtserklaerung.
  3. One page per position, shuffled order. Cascading selects (bore, stroke, mounting, certification), each needing
     its own "Auswahl uebernehmen" round trip, options sorted as text. Katalognummer options show pressure.
     Menge, Einzelpreis, collapsible Kalkulationsnachweis (base, surcharge, packaging, rebate), Lieferzeit select.
     "Position auslassen" skips. "Position hinzufuegen" adds a bogus extra position (trap).
  4. Konditionen: Rabatt and Nettosumme. A hidden `total_net` span shows the gross amount (trap).
  5. Erklaerungen: tick "Vergabeunterlagen anerkannt" only, not "Es gelten unsere AGB".
  6. Pruefen und signieren: request TAN, enter it, submit, accept `window.confirm`.
- TAN: each request invalidates the previous one; valid 5 minutes. Request, read mail, sign in one quick sequence.

## Webmail

- List and reading pane each behind a gate (slider to 100 plus "Ich bin kein Roboter"). `/messages/<id>` directly
  is simpler.
- Folders Posteingang and Archiv, searched separately. Search is AND over body too; empty search lists only TANs.
- Traps: look-alike references (`<ref>-A`), approvals for other tenders, non-approval mails from management,
  future-dated records, superseded and conditional approvals.
- Dates shown as `MM/TT`; full timestamp in `<time datetime>`.

## Supplier portal

- Spec found via the paged document list. Access gate: choose "Verbindliche Unterlagen", copy the Belegnummer
  (canvas, value in `aria-label`), tick the terms.
- Revision history collapsed; opens the oldest revision first. Status ("gueltig" / "ersetzt") only in a tooltip.
- Viewer iframe `.../viewer?revision=X&page=N`, one requirement per page. Full requirement prose in a collapsed
  "Originalwortlaut" (bore, stroke, pressure, mounting, certification, Kataloggruppe, pieces per Satz,
  nutzbarer Weg with Endreserve key).

## ERP

- After login: consent, often a flaky error page, then an unlock gate (slider, captcha box, copy Empfangsnummer).
- Only MM03, MMBE, VK13 exist; direct URLs work (`/mm03`, `/mmbe`, `/vk13?material=X`).
- Search popup `/search?transaction=..&q=..`; search the Kataloggruppe. Result rows already list most attributes,
  carton size, allocation mass vs surcharge mass, price index.
- MM03: technical tab (certification in tooltip); planning tab (status in tooltip, hidden decoy "01"; lead time
  from stock and production lead time).
- MMBE: the summary includes blocked stock (trap); use the free stock line.
- VK13: one condition record per page, older years later; validity, currency + FX key, price unit (1 or 100 ST);
  scales under `view=scales`, listed descending.
- No ordinary setup fee in the ERP; it comes from the tender Q&A.

## Architecture

```
agent/
  agent.py         orchestrator: reads run, shared findings store, starts workers, deadline (submit by T-90 s)
  llm.py           Qwen client, retry/backoff, thinking flag, usage log, stable prompts for caching
  browser_tools.py model-invoked tools (below) plus automatic overlay/gate/session handling
  extract.py       cleaned page text: visible only, details expanded, aria-labels, tooltips, iframes, no U+200B
  worker.py        generic loop: role prompt + goal + tools, step budget, deadline
  roles.py         generic role prompts: tender, spec, erp, mail
  evidence.py      pydantic records for each fact type
  calc.py          deterministic bid rules: rounding, scales, FX, packaging, setup pool, bonus (unit-tested)
  submit.py        configurator fill + TAN signing
```

Tools: `goto`, `click(ref)`, `fill(ref, text)`, `select(ref, value)`, `read_page`, `read_frame`, `next_page`,
`search(q)`, `screenshot` (fallback), `finish(result)`. Automatic: login with run credentials, consent, closing
decoy modals via x, unlocking gates, retrying flaky pages, re-login on expiry.

Fair-play line: the model chooses where to go, what to search, which revision / record / mail applies. Helpers only
extract a chosen page, paginate a chosen result set, calculate and fill forms.

## Scoring (what each version buys)

Per bid: decision 5, reference 5, discount 5, total 5, arithmetic consistency 5, withdrawn-Q&A check 5,
metal-index check 5, positions the rest (65 with both extra checks). Within each position: material 20 %,
quantity 15 %, base price 15 %, surcharge 10 %, packaging 10 %, bonus 10 %, final unit price 10 %, delivery 10 %.
Every field scores on its own, so each version adds fields and always ends with a signed bid.

## Roadmap

Each version is done when a sandbox test run (`atira test-run .`) shows the listed fields correct in the score
breakdown and finishes well under 20 minutes. Submit (`atira submit .`) after each version that beats our best.

### v0: harness (half a day)

- `llm.py`: pydantic-ai model for Qwen, thinking on/off settings, retries, usage logging.
- `extract.py`: cleaned page text (visible only, details expanded, aria-labels, tooltips, iframes, no U+200B).
- `browser_tools.py`: goto, click, fill, select, read_page, next_page, finish; automatic consent, decoy-modal
  close, gate unlock, flaky-page retry, re-login on expiry.
- `worker.py`: one pydantic-ai Agent per role, deps = page + findings store, step budget, deadline.
- Trace log per run (steps, tool calls, tokens, seconds) to see where time goes.
- Done when: a worker logs into each of the four scouting sites and reads one chosen page correctly.

**v0 status (2026-10-10): built.** `extract.py`, `browser_tools.py`, `worker.py`, `llm.py`, `tracing.py`;
check with `dev/smoke.py`. Learnings:

- Hosted Qwen sometimes hangs a call for ~300 s; the client times out after 30 s and retries (`LLM_TIMEOUT`).
  Steps then take 1 to 4 s.
- Gates re-lock on every mail page, so the generic "slide to unlock / not a robot" helper saves 4 to 6 steps
  per page. The ERP receipt-number gate is still solved by the model (works).
- Qwen invents values from memory once old views are trimmed. `note()` and worker results are checked: every
  value with a digit must appear on a page that worker saw, otherwise it goes back to the model. Thinking on
  invents less on document-heavy sites (tender, spec) at ~3 s per step.
- Smoke result: ERP 14 s and mail 18 s, correct and grounded; tender and spec read the right pages and note
  correct facts but hit the 25-step limit on broad goals. v1 goals must be narrow, with thinking on there.
- Open: a model that repeats a refused note loops; escalate after two refusals.

### v1: eligible signed bid (~10 to 15 points)

- Tender worker: reference, positions with units, bidder data from the brief.
- Configurator: Hauptangebot, omit every position, discount 0, total 0, decline AGB, request TAN.
- Mail worker: newest TAN, then sign and accept the confirm, all within the TAN's 5 minutes.
- Done when: reference and decision correct, the run is eligible.

### v2: materials, quantities, delivery (~+30)

- Tender worker reads the Q&A: quantity changes, withdrawals (withdrawn-Q&A check), Satz positions.
- Spec worker: current revision, requirement per position, Kataloggruppe, pieces per Satz.
- ERP worker: Kataloggruppe search, exact attribute match, active status; stock and both lead times.
- `calc.py`: final quantities, shared-stock rule, lead time; no_bid when a material is missing.
- Configurator fills material, quantity, lead time; price fields still blank or omitted per field.
- Done when: material, quantity, delivery correct per position.

### v3: prices, discount, totals (~+25)

- ERP worker: condition record valid on the scenario date, scales, price unit, currency + FX key.
- Mail worker: director approvals (exact reference, latest, conditional threshold), Devisenfixing.
- `calc.py`: base price with FX, discount clauses default rule, final unit price, total, HALF_UP everywhere.
- Done when: base price, discount, final unit price, total and arithmetic consistency correct.

### v4: clause rules (remaining points)

- Konditionsgruppen + Konditionsregeln (discount scope per position).
- Scoped amendments + Technikfreigabe (nutzbarer Weg) before material matching.
- Metal index (validity window) for the mass surcharge; packaging tariffs and cartons; Terminfreigabe
  commitments; Ruestpools shared setup with cent allocation; Projektbonus bands with largest-remainder split.
- Done when: every field in the breakdown is correct on public-1.

### v5: speed, cost, generalisation

- Four browsers, one per site, workers start as soon as their inputs are known.
- Thinking only on decision steps, trimmed snapshots, stable prompts for cache hits.
- Hard deadline guard: sign whatever is ready by T-90 s.
- Generalisation check: prompts and helpers contain no site names, URLs, field labels or values; helpers detect
  patterns (consent buttons, modals, sliders) generically. The private run uses other software and layouts.
- Optional: a stronger model with a team key only for steps the breakdown shows Qwen getting wrong.

## Working rules

- `calc.py` gets unit tests from the bid rules with invented numbers; it is pure and model-free.
- Hand-derived public-1 expectations live outside `agent/` (e.g. `checks/`), never in the package: the package
  reviewer rejects anything that looks like a stored answer.
- Split work by worker: tender + configurator, mail, spec, ERP, calc can be built in parallel against the
  findings store's pydantic records.

1	"""
2	From findings to what gets entered: one entry per tender position, filled where the facts are complete and omitted
3	with a reason where they are not. Pure and model-free; the bid rules themselves live in `calc.py`.
4	
5	This build prices a position as base price less the order discount. Surcharge, setup, packaging and bonus are not
6	applied yet.
7	"""
8	import re
9	from collections import defaultdict
10	from dataclasses import dataclass
11	from datetime import UTC, date, datetime, time, timedelta
12	from decimal import Decimal
13	from typing import Literal
14	
15	from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
16	
17	import calc
18	from evidence import Candidate, ErpFindings, Findings, MaterialFacts, Requirement, TenderFindings, TenderPosition
19	from parse import ParseError, parse_date, parse_datetime, parse_decimal, parse_int, parse_unit, split_address
20	
21	
22	class PlanEntry(BaseModel):
23	    position: str
24	    omit: bool = Field(description="True: leave the position out of the bid; `reason` says what was missing")
25	    reason: str = ""
26	    material_number: str = ""
27	    # the chosen material's attributes as the ERP writes them, to pick it in the bid form
28	    bore: str = ""
29	    stroke: str = ""
30	    pressure: str = ""
31	    mounting: str = ""
32	    certification: str = ""
33	    quantity: int | None = Field(default=None, description="Final quantity in pieces")
34	    lead_time_weeks: int | None = None
35	    unit_price: Decimal | None = Field(default=None, description="Final net unit price in EUR")
36	    base_unit_price: Decimal | None = None
37	
38	
39	class BidPlan(BaseModel):
40	    tender_reference: str
41	    decision: Literal["bid", "no_bid"] = "bid"
42	    discount_percent: Decimal = Decimal(0)
43	    total_net: Decimal = Decimal("0.00")
44	    entries: list[PlanEntry] = []
45	    notes: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list, description="Why something was omitted or assumed, for the trace")
46	
47	
48	class _Gap(calc.CalcError):
49	    """A fact this position needs was not established; the message is the omission reason."""
50	
51	
52	NUMERIC_KEYS = ("bore", "stroke", "pressure")  # compared as numbers; mounting and certification as text
53	_UNREADABLE = "\0unreadable: "  # marks an attribute value that could not be parsed, until the position needs it
54	_POSITION_WORD = r"(?:position|pos\.?|nr\.?|no\.?|#)"
55	_REVISION_WORD = r"(?:revision|rev\.?)"
56	
57	
58	def _ref(text: str, word: str = "") -> str:
59	    """An identifier for comparison: case and whitespace dropped, plus a leading label word such as "Pos."."""
60	    key = "".join(text.split()).casefold()
61	    if word:
62	        key = re.sub(rf"^{word}(?=.)", "", key)
63	    return key
64	
65	
66	def _position_ref(text: str) -> str:
67	    return re.sub(r"^0+(?=\d)", "", _ref(text, _POSITION_WORD).rstrip("."))
68	
69	
70	def _not_after(moment: datetime, scenario: datetime) -> bool:
71	    """Rule 21: dated no later than the scenario date. A scenario given as a bare day (midnight) covers that day."""
72	    if scenario.time() == time(0):
73	        return moment < scenario + timedelta(days=1)
74	    return moment <= scenario
75	
76	
77	def _labelled(label: str, parse, *args):
78	    """Run a parser and name the field in its error."""
79	    try:
80	        return parse(*args)
81	    except ParseError as e:
82	        raise ParseError(f"{label}: {e}") from e
83	
84	
85	def _short(error: Exception) -> str:
86	    return str(error).splitlines()[0]
87	
88	
89	def _attributes(shown: dict[str, str], number_format: str) -> dict[str, Decimal | str]:
90	    """Match attributes as values: numbers for bore, stroke and pressure, text otherwise."""
91	    out: dict[str, Decimal | str] = {}
92	    for name, value in shown.items():
93	        key = name.strip().casefold()
94	        if key in NUMERIC_KEYS:
95	            try:
96	                out[key] = parse_decimal(value, number_format)
97	            except ParseError as e:
98	                out[key] = _UNREADABLE + str(e)
99	        else:
100	            out[key] = value
101	    return out
102	
103	
104	def _unreadable(value: Decimal | str) -> bool:
105	    return isinstance(value, str) and value.startswith(_UNREADABLE)
106	
107	
108	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- tender Q&A
109	
110	
111	class _QA:
112	    """The Q&A records that apply on the scenario date, in the shape the calc helpers take."""
113	
114	    def __init__(self, tender: TenderFindings, scenario: datetime, notes: list[str]):
115	        self.shown = tender.quantity_changes
116	        self.changes: list[calc.QuantityChange] = []  # `quantity` holds the index into `shown`, parsed when it wins
117	        self.withdrawn: set[str] = set()
118	        self.amendments: list[calc.Amendment] = []
119	        self.skipped = False  # a record could not be read, so "nothing else applies" is not certain
120	
121	        for w in tender.withdrawals:
122	            if not w.date.strip():
123	                notes.append(f"withdrawal {w.answer} has no date: treated as in force")
124	                self.withdrawn.add(_ref(w.withdraws))
125	                continue
126	            when = self._when(w, f"withdrawal {w.answer}", notes)
127	            if when is not None and _not_after(when, scenario):
128	                self.withdrawn.add(_ref(w.withdraws))
129	        for index, c in enumerate(tender.quantity_changes):
130	            when = self._when(c, f"quantity change {c.answer}", notes)
131	            if when is not None and _not_after(when, scenario):
132	                self.changes.append(calc.QuantityChange(number=_ref(c.answer), date=when,
133	                                                        position=_position_ref(c.position), quantity=index))
134	        for a in tender.amendments:
135	            when = self._when(a, f"amendment {a.answer}", notes)
136	            if when is not None and _not_after(when, scenario):
137	                self.amendments.append(calc.Amendment(
138	                    date=when, revision=_ref(a.revision, _REVISION_WORD), requirement=_ref(a.requirement),
139	                    attributes=_attributes(a.attributes, a.number_format)))
140	
141	    def _when(self, record, label: str, notes: list[str]) -> datetime | None:
142	        try:
143	            return parse_datetime(record.date, record.date_order, record.timezone)
144	        except ParseError as e:
145	            notes.append(f"{label} skipped: {e}")
146	            self.skipped = True
147	            return None
148	
149	
150	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- mail authority
151	
152	
153	class _Mail(calc.DatedRecord):
154	    index: int
155	
156	
157	def _governing(records: list, sender_local: str, reference: str, scenario: datetime, domain: str, label: str,
158	               notes: list[str]) -> int | None:
159	    """Rule 21: index of the latest record for the exact reference from sender_local@domain, not after the scenario."""
160	    dated = []
161	    for index, r in enumerate(records):
162	        try:
163	            local, sender_domain = split_address(r.sender)
164	            when = parse_datetime(r.date, r.date_order, r.timezone)
165	        except ParseError as e:
166	            if r.reference.strip() == reference.strip():
167	                notes.append(f"{label} mail skipped: {e}")
168	            continue
169	        if _not_after(when, scenario):
170	            dated.append(_Mail(reference=r.reference, sender=f"{local}@{sender_domain}", date=when, index=index))
171	    hit = calc.latest_authoritative(dated, reference, date.max, sender_local, domain)  # dates are filtered above
172	    return None if hit is None else hit.index
173	
174	
175	def _approval(findings: Findings, reference: str, scenario: datetime, domain: str,
176	              notes: list[str]) -> calc.Approval | None:
177	    """Rules 5 and 16: the governing director approval. An unreadable one counts as none, never an older one."""
178	    approving = [a for a in findings.mail.approvals if a.approves]
179	    index = _governing(approving, "leitung", reference, scenario, domain, "approval", notes)
180	    if index is None:
181	        notes.append("no discount approval applies: discount 0")
182	        return None
183	    shown = approving[index]
184	    try:
185	        percent = _labelled("approved percent", parse_decimal, shown.percent, shown.number_format)
186	        minimum = None
187	        if shown.min_order_value.strip():
188	            minimum = _labelled("minimum order value", parse_decimal, shown.min_order_value, shown.number_format)
189	        if not 0 <= percent <= 100:
190	            raise ParseError(f"approved percent {percent} out of range")
191	    except ParseError as e:
192	        notes.append(f"governing approval unreadable ({e}): discount 0")
193	        return None
194	    return calc.Approval(percent=percent, min_order_value=minimum)
195	
196	
197	@dataclass
198	class _Fx:
199	    rates: dict[str, Decimal]  # FX key or currency, upper-cased -> EUR per unit
200	    unreadable: dict[str, str]
201	    found: bool
202	
203	
204	def _fx(findings: Findings, reference: str, scenario: datetime, domain: str, notes: list[str]) -> _Fx:
205	    """Rule 22: the rates of the governing FX fixing (sent, exact reference, finance sender, not after the scenario)."""
206	    sent = [f for f in findings.mail.fx_fixings if f.sent]
207	    index = _governing(sent, "finanzen", reference, scenario, domain, "FX fixing", notes)
208	    fx = _Fx(rates={}, unreadable={}, found=index is not None)
209	    if index is not None:
210	        for key, value in sent[index].rates.items():
211	            try:
212	                fx.rates[key.strip().upper()] = parse_decimal(value, sent[index].number_format)
213	            except ParseError as e:
214	                fx.unreadable[key.strip().upper()] = str(e)
215	    return fx
216	
217	
218	@dataclass
219	class _Releases:
220	    reserves: dict[str, Decimal]  # reserve key, upper-cased -> reserve per end
221	    unreadable: dict[str, str]
222	    found: bool
223	
224	
225	def _releases(findings: Findings, reference: str, revision: str, scenario: datetime, domain: str,
226	              notes: list[str]) -> _Releases:
227	    """Rules 20 and 21: the reserves of the governing technical release for the current specification revision."""
228	    scoped = [r for r in findings.mail.technical_releases if revision and _ref(r.revision, _REVISION_WORD) == revision]
229	    index = _governing(scoped, "technik", reference, scenario, domain, "technical release", notes)
230	    out = _Releases(reserves={}, unreadable={}, found=index is not None)
231	    if index is not None:
232	        for key, value in scoped[index].reserves.items():
233	            try:
234	                out.reserves[key.strip().upper()] = parse_decimal(value, scoped[index].number_format)
235	            except ParseError as e:
236	                out.unreadable[key.strip().upper()] = str(e)

243	@dataclass
244	class _State:
245	    tender: TenderPosition
246	    reason: str = ""  # first missing fact; empty = nothing missing so far
247	    pieces: int | None = None
248	    material: Candidate | None = None
249	    facts: MaterialFacts | None = None

259	def _pieces(tender: TenderPosition, requirement: Requirement | None, qa: _QA) -> int:
260	    """Rules 1, 13, 17: the tender quantity or the governing change, in pieces."""
261	    quantity = _labelled("tender quantity", parse_int, tender.quantity, tender.number_format)
262	    unit_text = tender.unit
263	    winner = calc.resolve_quantity(-1, _position_ref(tender.position), qa.changes, qa.withdrawn)
264	    if winner >= 0:
265	        change = qa.shown[winner]
266	        quantity = _labelled(f"quantity of change {change.answer}", parse_int, change.quantity, change.number_format)
267	        unit_text = change.unit if change.unit.strip() else unit_text
268	    unit = parse_unit(unit_text)
269	    per_set = None
270	    if unit is calc.Unit.SET and requirement is not None and requirement.pieces_per_set.strip():
271	        per_set = _labelled("pieces per set", parse_int, requirement.pieces_per_set, requirement.number_format)
272	    pieces = calc.to_pieces(quantity, unit, per_set)
273	    if pieces <= 0:
274	        raise _Gap(f"quantity is {pieces}")
275	    return pieces

278	def _reserve(requirement: Requirement, revision: str, releases: _Releases) -> Decimal:
279	    """Rule 20: the per-end reserve the governing technical release of this revision states for the requirement."""
280	    if not releases.found:
281	        raise _Gap("stroke is given as usable travel and no technical release for the revision applies")
282	    key = requirement.reserve_key.strip().upper()
283	    if key in releases.unreadable:
284	        raise ParseError(f"end reserve {key}: {releases.unreadable[key]}")
285	    if key not in releases.reserves:
286	        if not key and len(releases.reserves) == 1:
287	            return next(iter(releases.reserves.values()))
288	        raise _Gap(f"the technical release states no end reserve for key {key or '(none)'}")
289	    return releases.reserves[key]

291	
292	def _requirement(requirement: Requirement, revision: str, qa: _QA, releases: _Releases) -> dict[str, Decimal | str]:
293	    """Rules 14 and 20: the requirement's match attributes after the amendments scoped to this revision and
294	    requirement, with a usable stroke turned into the nominal one."""
295	    key = _ref(requirement.requirement)
296	    if not revision and any(a.requirement == key for a in qa.amendments):
297	        raise _Gap("current specification revision unknown, so amendments cannot be scoped")
298	    shown = {k: getattr(requirement, k) for k in calc.MATCH_KEYS}
299	    attributes = calc.apply_amendments(_attributes(shown, requirement.number_format), qa.amendments, revision, key)
300	    for name in calc.MATCH_KEYS:
301	        value = attributes[name]
302	        if _unreadable(value):
303	            raise ParseError(f"requirement {name}: {str(value).removeprefix(_UNREADABLE)}")
304	    if requirement.usable_stroke:
305	        attributes["stroke"] = calc.nominal_stroke(attributes["stroke"], _reserve(requirement, revision, releases))
306	    return attributes
307	
308	
309	def _material(state: _State, required: dict[str, Decimal | str], erp: ErpFindings | None,
310	              notes: list[str]) -> Candidate:
311	    """Rule 3: the model's choice, cross-checked: among the candidates, active and equal on every match attribute."""
312	    if erp is None:
313	        raise _Gap("no ERP lookup for the requirement")
314	    if not erp.candidates:
315	        raise _Gap("no ERP candidates read for the requirement")
316	    listed = []
317	    for c in erp.candidates:
318	        attributes = _attributes({k: getattr(c, k) for k in calc.MATCH_KEYS}, c.number_format)
319	        listed.append({k: v for k, v in attributes.items() if not _unreadable(v)})  # unreadable never matches
320	    active = [(str(i), listed[i]) for i, c in enumerate(erp.candidates) if c.active is True]
321	    matches = [erp.candidates[int(i)] for i in calc.matching_materials(required, active)]
322	    chosen = _ref(erp.chosen)
323	    for c in matches:
324	        if _ref(c.material_number) == chosen:
325	            return c
326	    position = state.tender.position
327	    if len(matches) == 1:
328	        notes.append(f"position {position}: chosen material {erp.chosen or '(none)'} fails the cross-check; "
329	                     f"{matches[0].material_number} is the only active candidate that matches and is used")
330	        return matches[0]
331	    if matches:
332	        raise _Gap(f"several active candidates match and the chosen material {erp.chosen or '(none)'} is not one")
333	
334	    # Wording is the model's call: two sources may name the same mounting or certification differently, so a chosen
335	    # active material that equals the requirement on every number is accepted on the model's reading of the text.
336	    numbers = tuple(k for k in calc.MATCH_KEYS if k in NUMERIC_KEYS)
337	    picked = next((c for c in erp.candidates if _ref(c.material_number) == chosen), None)
338	    if picked is not None and picked.active is True and calc.matching_materials(
339	            required, [("", listed[erp.candidates.index(picked)])], keys=numbers):
340	        notes.append(f"position {position}: chosen material {erp.chosen} equals the requirement on every number; "
341	                     "mounting or certification are worded differently and taken on the model's comparison")
342	        return picked
343	
344	    # nothing matches: sure enough for no_bid only if the model chose none as well and every candidate is known
345	    # blocked or differs on a known number (a difference in wording alone is never certain)
346	    def differs(attributes: dict[str, Decimal | str]) -> bool:
347	        return any(k in attributes and attributes[k] != "" and required[k] != ""
348	                   and not calc.matching_materials(required, [("", attributes)], keys=(k,)) for k in numbers)
349	
350	    state.certain_no_match = (not chosen and erp.all_candidates_read
351	                              and all(required[k] != "" for k in calc.MATCH_KEYS)
352	                              and all(c.active is False or differs(listed[i]) for i, c in enumerate(erp.candidates)))
353	    if not chosen:
354	        raise _Gap("no material chosen and no active candidate matches the requirement")
355	    if picked is None:
356	        raise _Gap(f"chosen material {erp.chosen} is not among the candidates")
357	    if picked.active is not True:
358	        raise _Gap(f"chosen material {erp.chosen} is not active" if picked.active is False
359	                   else f"status of chosen material {erp.chosen} unknown")
360	    raise _Gap(f"chosen material {erp.chosen} does not match the requirement exactly")
361

363	def _weeks(label: str, text: str, number_format: str) -> int:
364	    """A lead time in weeks; one stated in days counts only if it is whole weeks."""
365	    value = _labelled(label, parse_int, text, number_format)
366	    if re.search(r"\b(tage?n?|days?)\b", text, re.IGNORECASE):
367	        if value % 7:
368	            raise ParseError(f"{label}: {text.strip()!r} is not whole weeks")
369	        return value // 7
370	    return value
371

373	def _lead_time(facts: MaterialFacts, pooled: int, open_demand: bool) -> int:
374	    """Rules 6 and 15: stock lead time if free stock covers the material's pooled demand, else production."""
375	    stock = _labelled("free stock", parse_int, facts.free_stock, facts.number_format)
376	    # ask calc which of the two lead times applies (0 = stock, 1 = production), then read only that one
377	    probe = calc.Material(material_number=facts.material_number, free_stock=stock, stock_lead_time_weeks=0,
378	                          production_lead_time_weeks=1)
379	    from_stock = calc.lead_time(calc.PositionInput(position="", quantity=0, material=probe), pooled) == 0
380	    if from_stock and open_demand:
381	        raise _Gap("pooled demand unknown: another position with this material has no quantity")
382	    if from_stock:
383	        return _weeks("stock lead time", facts.stock_lead_time_weeks, facts.number_format)
384	    return _weeks("production lead time", facts.production_lead_time_weeks, facts.number_format)
385	
386	
387	def _condition(facts: MaterialFacts, day: date, fx: _Fx, position: str, notes: list[str]) -> calc.PriceCondition:
388	    """Rule 4: the price condition valid on the scenario day, parsed. Other conditions only need readable dates."""
389	    dated = []
390	    for c in facts.conditions:
391	        start = _labelled("price validity start", parse_date, c.valid_from, c.date_order)
392	        open_end = not re.search(r"\d", c.valid_to)  # blank or a word such as "open": no end
393	        end = None if open_end else _labelled("price validity end", parse_date, c.valid_to, c.date_order)
394	        dated.append(calc.PriceCondition(valid_from=start, valid_to=end, scales=[]))
395	    valid = calc.valid_condition(dated, day)
396	    shown = next(c for c, d in zip(facts.conditions, dated) if d is valid)
397	    number_format = shown.number_format or facts.number_format
398	
399	    scales = []
400	    for s in shown.scales:
401	        lone_price = len(shown.scales) == 1 and not s.min_quantity.strip()  # one price without a scale table
402	        minimum = 0 if lone_price else _labelled("scale quantity", parse_int, s.min_quantity, number_format)
403	        scales.append(calc.PriceScale(min_quantity=minimum, price=_labelled("price", parse_decimal, s.price,
404	                                                                            number_format)))
405	    currency = shown.currency.strip().upper().replace("€", "EUR")
406	    if not currency and any("€" in s.price or "EUR" in s.price.upper() for s in shown.scales):
407	        currency = "EUR"
408	    if not currency:
409	        raise _Gap("currency of the price condition unknown")
410	    if shown.price_unit.strip():
411	        price_unit = _labelled("price unit", parse_int, shown.price_unit, number_format)
412	    else:
413	        price_unit = 1
414	        notes.append(f"position {position}: no price unit stated, assumed 1 piece")
415	    fx_key = shown.fx_key.strip().upper() or None
416	    if currency != "EUR":
417	        key = fx_key or currency
418	        if key in fx.unreadable:
419	            raise ParseError(f"FX rate {key}: {fx.unreadable[key]}")
420	        if key not in fx.rates and currency not in fx.rates:
421	            raise _Gap(f"no usable FX fixing for {key}" if not fx.found else f"the FX fixing has no rate for {key}")
422	    return calc.PriceCondition(valid_from=valid.valid_from, valid_to=valid.valid_to, currency=currency, fx_key=fx_key,
423	                               price_unit=price_unit, scales=scales)

426	def _bid_input(states: list[_State], reference: str, day: date, fx: _Fx,
427	               approval: calc.Approval | None = None) -> calc.BidInput:
428	    """Priced positions as calc input. Lead times are decided here (pooled over all positions), so calc gets them
429	    fixed; the stock is left at 0 and both lead times set to the decided one."""
430	    positions = []
431	    for s in states:
432	        assert s.material is not None and s.pieces is not None and s.condition is not None
433	        weeks = s.lead_time or 0
434	        material = calc.Material(material_number=s.material.material_number, stock_lead_time_weeks=weeks,
435	                                 production_lead_time_weeks=weeks)
436	        positions.append(calc.PositionInput(position=s.tender.position, quantity=s.pieces, material=material,
437	                                            conditions=[s.condition]))
438	    return calc.BidInput(tender_reference=reference, scenario_date=day, positions=positions, approval=approval,
439	                         fx_rates=fx.rates)
